Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork "JusPrin"). Work in the worktree this session gives you; do not touch the main checkout. First `git fetch origin` and base your branch on origin/jusprin-newui (336facf825 or later). Another task (`task_98ae90ed`) is changing how the workspace snapshot is placed in the user message in `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input`; this task is about `AgentHost::make_agent_request`, so the two should not overlap, but expect a small merge in AgentHost.cpp.

## The problem

`AgentHost::make_agent_request` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp, the block that builds `request.conversation`) replays each earlier message and, after each assistant message, the tool calls it made with their results, one entry per call-plus-result so a call is never sent without its output. A result over 16 KiB (`kReplayedResultCap`) is replaced by an omission note that tells the model to call the tool again. Then `kHistoryMessages = 20` keeps the last 20 entries, counting a replayed call as one, by erasing from the front. The history is sent to the model on every request with `store:false`, so this is the model's whole memory of the chat.

Trimming the oldest entries regardless of kind has the wrong order of loss. A busy turn with ten tool calls leaves ten entries of actual conversation. Older tool payloads of up to 16 KiB each survive while the person's and the assistant's words from earlier in the chat are dropped. Anthropic's context-engineering guidance says the safe, light form of compaction is clearing old tool calls and results; the conversation text is what to keep. The 2026-09-24 commit 115e2776bf, which introduced the replay, already notes that "trimming is done selectively" and that a large result "is not worth its space on every later turn: the model keeps the outcome and may ask for the details again".

## What to do

Replace the single entry-count cut with staged trimming, in this order, stopping as soon as the budget is met:

1. Replace tool results older than the last two assistant turns with the existing omission note (same JSON shape: state plus the "not repeated here; call the tool again" text), keeping the call itself so the model still knows what it did and with what arguments.
2. If still over budget, drop whole call-plus-result pairs, oldest first.
3. If still over budget, drop the oldest text entries.

Define the budget in bytes of the serialized conversation entries, not in entry count, with a constant you justify in a comment from what the provider's cache and the 16 KiB cap imply (the old 20-entry cap allowed up to about 320 KiB of results, which was never the intent; something in the range of 48 to 96 KiB is the likely answer, but measure a real chat's entries before choosing). Keep the invariant that a call is never sent without its output and never an output without its call. Keep file-load reports in history as they are (they are text entries with their own boundary line). Do not change what `OpenAIResponsesAgent` does with the entries. Keep the change small: this should be a few dozen lines in one function plus tests, not a new module.

## Verification

Tests live in tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp (grep for kHistoryMessages, "replay", "omitted" to find the existing ones). Update them and add: a chat with many tool calls where the conversation text survives and old results become omission notes; a chat where pairs are dropped before text; the call-with-output invariant under every stage; and the budget boundary. Build and run agent_bridge_tests (recipe: /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/jusprin-worktree-build.md; CMake from /Applications/CMake.app; reuse existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON; long builds with nohup and a log, never as a background Bash command). No live model call.

Commit on a branch in your worktree with a plain-English message; do not push. Write an untracked report in the worktree root (never commit it, never add it to .gitignore) for an engineer who did not see this session: the old and new trimming rule side by side, the budget you chose and the measurement behind it, and one worked example showing which entries a 30-entry chat keeps under each rule. Plain English, no label-colon fragments; Kenneth reads these.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

I found solid documentation on the 1024-token threshold and 128-token increments, but nothing that directly says whether `store: false` affects caching.

**Threshold and increments:** Caching applies automatically to prompts of 1024 tokens or more. The system caches in 128-token increments beyond the initial 1,024 tokens. A community post works out the consequence: the number of cached tokens for a request will always follow this sequence: 1024, 1152, 1280, 1408, and so on.

**Matching and routing:** Caching only works if two requests share the same prefix and land on the same machine. OpenAI's cookbook notes that the optional parameter `prompt_cache_key` can improve routing for traffic that shares common prefixes. The prefix covers more than messages: messages, images, audio, tool definitions, and structured output schemas.

**Retention:** Cached prefixes generally remain active for 5 to 10 minutes of inactivity. However, during off-peak periods, caches may persist for up to one hour. For longer retention, the Responses API reference says that setting 24h enables extended prompt caching, which keeps cached prefixes active for longer, up to a maximum of 24 hours.

**Monitoring:** Hits show up in the response usage object as cached_tokens under prompt token details.

**`store: false`:** The results don't say that `store: false` disables or changes prompt caching. The only `store: false` references in the OpenAI docs concern reasoning items. The Responses reference says reasoning items can be used in multi-turn conversations when using the Responses API statelessly (like when the store parameter is set to false). A cookbook example says that reasoning items from turn 1 are ignored and removed in turn 2, since the model does not reuse reasoning items from previous turns. As a result, a fourth API call cannot achieve a full cache hit, because those reasoning items are missing from the prompt. So if you send history statelessly, keep that in mind when expecting full hits. A NVIDIA relay doc describes its own cache bypass for stored requests, but that is a third-party proxy behavior, not OpenAI's caching rule. Check OpenAI's prompt caching guide directly to confirm.

**Conflicting reports on the API:** Sources disagree on which API caches best. One site says Chat completions don't support full caching, while the cookbook reports that switching from the Completions API to the Responses API boosted cache utilization from 40% to 80% in its tests. A community test found that Responses without `previous_response_id` had the worst results. These are older or anecdotal, so test against your own traffic.

# Chat history trimming by size

Branch `claude/staged-history-trim`, commit 92fd35769e on origin/jusprin-newui 336facf825. Not pushed.

## The problem

Every request the app sends to the model carries the earlier chat, because requests use `store:false` and the provider remembers nothing between them. `AgentHost::make_agent_request` builds that history: each earlier message, and after each assistant message the tool calls it made, each call with its result as one entry. It then kept the last 20 entries and erased the rest from the front.

That cut lost things in the wrong order. A turn with ten tool calls filled half the window with tool payloads, each up to 16 KiB, and pushed out what the person and the assistant had said a few turns earlier. Twenty entries could also reach about 320 KiB, which nobody intended.

## Old rule and new rule

| | Old rule | New rule |
|---|---|---|
| Limit | 20 entries | 64 KiB of serialized entries |
| When it trims | Whenever there are more than 20 entries | Only when the history is over 64 KiB |
| What goes first | The oldest entry, whatever it is | Results of calls older than the last two assistant turns, oldest first, replaced by the existing "not repeated here; call the tool again" note. The call and its arguments stay. |
| What goes next | (same) | Whole calls with their results, oldest first, including recent ones |
| What goes last | (same) | The oldest words. The newest message is always kept, even if it alone is over the budget. |

Each stage stops as soon as the history fits. A turn means every assistant message answering one message: after a tool call, the reply is a new assistant message with the same `in_reply_to`. A call and its result are still one entry, so neither can be sent without the other. File-load reports are text entries and are treated like any other words.

## The budget and how I chose it

I measured twelve live 3-turn project chats recorded on 2026-10-12 with real tool results (the model-probe transcripts in the `model-nature-probe` worktree). Replayed the way the app replays them, each chat came to 9 to 33 KB (median about 20 KB). None of the 87 tool results was over 10 KB. The largest were `object_analyze` and `settings_search`, at about 9 KB each. Most results were under 1 KB. The project-prompt recordings (2,599 real tool outputs) agree: the largest was 4.2 KB.

64 KiB is roughly 16,000 to 20,000 tokens. That is enough for two recent turns that each returned two results at the 16 KiB cap, and at the measured rate of about 7 KB per turn, a typical chat runs about ten turns before anything is trimmed. The provider caches the unchanged start of a request. Any trimmed entry changes everything after it, so trimming rarely, and from the oldest end, keeps most of the history cached. The old rule shifted the whole window on every turn once a chat passed 20 entries.

## Worked example: 30 entries

Ten turns, each made of the person's message (300 characters), one tool call, and the assistant's reply (500 characters). The results are realistic sizes: turn 1 `workspace_inspect` 4 KB, turns 2, 5 and 9 `object_analyze` 9 KB, turns 3, 6 and 10 `settings_search` 9 KB, turn 4 a 22 KB `settings_get` (already over the 16 KiB cap, so it is replayed as the note), turn 7 `slice_start` 0.3 KB, and turn 8 `slice_report` 2.3 KB. That comes to 73 KB in all. I computed this with a script that applies both rules, not with the app.

The old rule keeps entries 11 to 30, about 47 KB. Turns 1 to 3 disappear completely. Turn 4 keeps its call and reply but loses the person's message that led to them.

The new rule keeps all 30 entries, about 60 KB. Only the results of turns 1 and 2 become the note. Every message from both sides survives, and so does every call with its arguments.

## Tests and results
